t:
Title VI of the Public Health Service Act is amended by inserting immediately after section 623 the following new section:


“loans for certain hospital experimentation projects
“Sec. 623A. 

(a) 
In order to alleviate hardship on any recipient of a grant under section 636 of this title (as in effect immediately before the enactment of the Hospital and Medical Facilities Amendments of 1964) for a project for the construction of an experimental or demonstration facility having as its specific purpose the application of novel means for the reduction of hospital costs with respect to which there has been a substantial increase in the cost of such construction (over the estimated cost of such project on the basis of which such grant was made) through no fault of such recipient, the Secretary is authorized to make a loan to such recipient not exceeding 66⅔ per centum of such increased costs, as determined by the Secretary, if the Secretary determines that such recipient is unable to obtain such an amount for such purpose from other public or private sources.


“(b) 
Any such loan shall be made only on the basis of an application submitted to the Secretary in such form and containing such information and assurances as he may prescribe.


“(c) 
Each such loan shall bear interest at the rate of 2½ per centum per annum on the unpaid balance thereof and shall be repayable over a period determined by the Secretary to be appropriate, mt not exceeding fifty years.


“(d) 
There are hereby authorized to be appropriated $3,500,000 to carry out the provisions of this section.”

fable.w: The section authorizes federal loans to existing grant recipients for increased hospital construction costs, made on the basis of an application to the Secretary. The tempting reading is that an outside party (the recipient) interacts with the Secretary, or that "as he may prescribe" implies rulemaking. But applying for a loan is an application for a benefit, not participation in a federal decision, and prescribing an application form is not a regulation or comment process. There is no hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: Any such loan shall be made only on the basis of an application submitted to the Secretary in such form and containing such information and assurances as he may prescribe.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a loan program where recipients must submit applications to the Secretary. The definition explicitly states that 'applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses' are not considered participation. The process described is a standard administrative application for financial assistance, not a consultation or coordination with outside parties regarding a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: Any such loan shall be made only on the basis of an application submitted to the Secretary in such form and containing such information and assurances as he may prescribe.

opus.w: The only outside-party interaction in this section is a grant recipient applying for a loan. Applying for a benefit is expressly excluded from participation. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with states or others, rulemaking, or a right to sue. The Secretary's power to prescribe the form of the application is administrative and does not bring outsiders into a federal policy decision.
opus.s: Any such loan shall be made only on the basis of an application submitted to the Secretary in such form and containing such information and assurances as he may prescribe.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that subsection (b) counts as participation, because an outside party (the grant recipient) submits an application to the Secretary. It doesn't. The definition excludes applications for benefits, grants, contracts or licenses, and this is an application for a loan, which is a financial benefit. The phrase "as he may prescribe" only lets the Secretary set the form of the application. It is not a grant of rulemaking authority.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a loan program where recipients must submit applications to receive funds. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' Since a loan application is analogous to a grant application in this context, it does not constitute participation. The interaction is limited to the administrative process of applying for financial assistance, not consulting on or influencing a federal policy decision.
qwen_chat.s: Any such loan shall be made only on the basis of an application submitted to the Secretary in such form and containing such information and assurances as he may prescribe.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for an application involves interaction with the government, but the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" (and by extension, loans) from the scope of participation. The process described is purely administrative for the recipient to obtain funds, not a mechanism for outside parties to influence federal decision-making through consultation, advisory roles, or public comment.
